subject: Protected managed-MCP-runtime install: retained partial attempt and prepared reconciliation

root_cause.defect: operator umask 0o077 stripped group/other bits from mkdir(mode=0o755); the explicit chmod covered only regular files
root_cause.failure_mechanism: the UID-992 proof child could not read pm-runtime/pm-runtime.json (EACCES), exited nonzero, and the installer require() raised ValueError
root_cause.content_impact: none: every archive member, its digests, the pm-runtime marker and the merged facts.json published correctly
downstream_checks_confirmed_safe: verified_tools is explicitly read-only and takes no install lock
the absent python/.install.lock is writer-side state; readers do not require it
tree_digest covers relpath and content only, never mode bits, so mode correction cannot disturb recorded digests

design: refuses unless the retained v1 summary is the known publication-stage partial or the v2 summary is the known verification-stage refusal
verifies the pinned v1 installer source hash before reusing its code
re-admits the sealed archive (hash, admission, per-file digests) and verifies the published payload member-by-member, refusing any unexpected file, mode, owner or entry
verifies the merged live facts.json bytes separately instead of comparing them to the archive's staged copy
walks only the three payload subtrees; the store root legitimately keeps pre-release tools (ffmpeg, node, npm, ripgrep)
corrects only payload directory modes to their archived 0755 values and re-verifies
reruns the identical restricted-identity proof with stdout/stderr captured into the artifact regardless of outcome
records its receipt under operator-managed-mcp-runtime-v3; the v1 partial publication and the v2 verification refusal stay retained and untouched
idempotent on its own completed receipt; never retries a failed attempt automatically

dry_run_readonly_stages.walk_root_coverage: no archive member lies outside the payload subtrees

operator-managed-mcp-runtime-v2.cause: the first revision wrongly size/hash-compared the merged live facts.json against the archive's staged copy, and its tree walk covered the whole store, flagging legitimate pre-release tools as unexpected entries
